question.problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{9x-3y}.
$$

The general solution to this equation can be expressed in the form

$$
\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|g(x,y)|=y+C,
$$

where $C$ is a constant. What is $g(x,y)?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we factor the right-hand side of the given equation.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2}{3(3x-y)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we make the substitution

$$
z=3x-y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=3-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3-\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3-\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2}{3z}\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z)$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=\frac{9z-2}{3z}.
$$

This differential equation is separable. So, we separate the variables and integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3z}{9z-2}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int \frac{3z}{9z-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int \text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{3}\int (1+\frac{2}{9z-2})\text{d}z & =\int \text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{3}(z+\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|9z-2|) & =x+K \\ z+\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|9z-2| & =3x+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=3K.$

Finally, we write the equation in terms of $y$ and $x$ using our original substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-y+\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|27x-9y-2| & =3x+C \\ \frac{2}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|27x-9y-2| & =y+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
g(x,y)=27x-9y-2.
$$
